newsitem.title: USA: Blimpie sees FY 1997 earnings below 1996.
newsitem.headline: Blimpie sees FY 1997 earnings below 1996.

text.p: Blimpie International Inc said on Monday that it expects to report earnings per share for fiscal 1997 that are $0.07 or $0.08 below the $0.41 per share it earned the year before.

But Blimpie Chairman Anthony Conza said in an interview that a major overseas expansion program, the company's first national television campaign and some possible acquisitions should position the company for longer-term growth.
"I think this is probably as low as it's going to get," Conza said of the earnings for fiscal 1997, which ends June 30.
Conza said he expects this trend of falling short of the previous period's earnings to continue "for several more quarters," but he also sees the performance gap narrowing quarter by quarter in 1998.

He said the company posted eight years of record earnings through 1996 in part because it was growing from a regional to a national brand by selling territorial licenses. Now, with Blimpie in 49 states, that source of income is drying up, contributing to the decline in earnings growth, he said.
But, with franchisees now opening 25 to 30 new Blimpie restaurants each month, the company's income from continuing fees is rising, Conza said.
"As long as that revenue stream continues to increase, our earnings are going to increase," he said.

Blimpie also is pursuing overseas expansion. The company on Monday said it expanding to Jordan, Peru, the Dominican Republic, Poland, Cyprus and South Africa, bringing the number of foreign countries in which it has a presence to 11.
"By the end of this year we'll be in about 15," Conza said.
Blimpie now has about 1,700 restaurants. Within five years it plans to have 5,000, including 500 in foreign countries.
"In five years, I would guess that 15 percent to 20 percent of our revenues will come from overseas," Conza said.

Blimpie also plans to double its advertising budget in calendar 1997, to $11 million. That will include the company's first national television campaign, featuring Conza, its founder, in spots that will run on ESPN.
"We're putting a heavy emphasis on marketing and advertising, something that we've never done in the past," he said.

Blimpie earlier this year hired BC Capital Corp to advise it on potential acquisitions. Conza said none has been identified yet, but the company is actively looking at other food companies that it could co-brand with Blimpie, with both brands sharing locations.
Conza said his industry is so competitive these days that a shakeout is inevitable.
"There's going to be a consolidation," he said, and Blimpie would rather make a meal of another company than be eaten itself. "We have no ambitions to be acquired at this time," he said.
